newsitem.title: USA: Des Plaines, Ill., debt AA-minus - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Des Plaines, Ill., debt AA-minus - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Oct 21 - Standard & Poor's Corp today said has assigned its double-A'-minus ratings to Des Plaines, Ill.'s $9.5 million G.O. refunding bonds series 1996A and $500,000 G.O. tax increment finance taxable refunding bonds series 1996B, which are both scheduled to sell Oct. 21, 1996.
In addition, Standard & Poor's has assigned its double-A'-minus rating to the city's nontaxable G.O. parity debt and taxable G.O. parity debt.
-- Favorable location within the Chicago, Ill. area,
-- Modestly growing and diverse property tax base,
-- Diverse revenue stream and improved reserve levels,
-- Somewhat-above-average wealth and income levels, and
These strengths ARE offset by declines in one of the city's major revenue source, sales tax revenues, which indicates a susceptibility in the local economic base.

Des Plaines, with a population of 53,000, lies northwest of Chicago adjacent to the O'Hare airport. Although almost fully developed, the property tax base has been growing modestly, averaging 5.6% annually from 1987-1996. However, sales tax revenues declined in the early 1990s and although receipts have recovered, 1995 revenues were 15% less than 1990 revenues. Declines in sales tax revenues led to drawdowns in general fund balance reserve levels. To counteract the impact of the decline in sales tax revenues and to restore a structural balance to the budget, the city instituted various revenue enhancements and expenditure cuts. Although the city did not raise property taxes substantially, it increased or instituted various taxes, including a utility tax and motor fuel tax.

These measures enabled the city to end fiscal 1995 with a general fund balance of $3.6 million, or 16% of general fund expenditures. An increase in the balance of about $2 million is projected for fiscal 1996, and fiscal 1997 is budgeted with a slight surplus. Current balances show an improvement over fiscal 1993-1994, when balances fell below $2 million, but are on par with levels maintained prior to the city's fiscal problems. Revenues are a good mix of property, income, and sales taxes. Major expenditure categories include public safety, public works, general government, and debt service. The property tax base is a good mix of residential, commercial, and industrial properties. Residents have above-average wealth and income levels with per capita money income 116% of the county and 129% of U.S. average.

Bond proceeds will be used to refund a portion of the city's outstanding bonds. Debt levels are manageable at $1,852 per capita and 2.5% of market value. Total direct debt of the city is $30.48 million. Although additional debt is anticipated, debt ratios are not expected to change significantly.
The outlook reflects the expectation that the city will maintain strong reserve levels, Standard & Poor's said.
